tracks.title: Family
tracks.blurb: Warm catch-ups with family she already knows: door hellos, New Year, dinner, teasing Shota, video calls.

tracks.title: Getting around
tracks.blurb: Trains and asking for help first, then cafés, shops, and the konbini.

units.title: Seeing them again
units.summary: Warm hellos when you walk back into Shota's family home: catching up, offering help, light teasing — not a first meeting.

phrases.kana: ひさしぶりです
phrases.note: Warm and polite for his parents when you haven't seen them in a bit. Casual with siblings/peers: 久しぶり！

phrases.jp: また会えてうれしいです
phrases.kana: またあえてうれしいです
phrases.en: I'm so happy to see you again.
phrases.note: Returning-visitor warmth. Skip はじめまして — you already know each other.

phrases.kana: おじゃまします
phrases.en: Thanks for having me (as you enter)
phrases.note: Still the right door phrase even when you're a familiar guest. Soften with a smile.

phrases.kana: おげんきでしたか
phrases.note: Natural catch-up after time apart. They may answer casually; you can stay in です/ます.

phrases.jp: はい、元気です。お父さんは？
phrases.kana: はい、げんきです。おとうさんは？
phrases.note: Confirmed: お父さん / お母さん for his parents. Ending with は？ means "and you / and him?".

phrases.jp: 何かお手伝いしましょうか
phrases.kana: なにかおてつだいしましょうか
phrases.note: Offer this in the kitchen — they often say 大丈夫, but offering matters.

phrases.jp: しょうた、また寝てるんですか
phrases.kana: しょうた、またねてるんですか
phrases.romaji: Shōta, mata neteru n desu ka
phrases.note: Light teasing about Shota. Soften with a laugh; parents usually love it.

phrases.jp: アーバインとソウル出身です
phrases.kana: アーバインとソウルしゅっしんです
phrases.note: Confirmed hometowns. Optional native/Shota check: ソウルで生まれて、アーバインで育ちました (born in Seoul, grew up in Irvine) — not confirmed yet.

phrases.jp: 今日もよろしくお願いします
phrases.kana: きょうもよろしくおねがいします
phrases.en: Looking forward to today (with you again).
phrases.note: A returning-visit closer — も ("again / also") marks that you're back.

units.title: New Year & holidays
units.summary: A warm visit over New Year or another family holiday: the greeting, a small gift, osechi and mochi, and a real thank-you. You already know them.

phrases.jp: あけましておめでとう
phrases.note: How you greet お父さん and お母さん on New Year's day. Familiar, not a speech.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.jp: 今年もよろしくお願いします
phrases.kana: ことしもよろしくおねがいします
phrases.en: Let's have another good year together
phrases.note: Say it right after the New Year greeting. They may answer 今年もよろしく.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.jp: これ、よかったらどうぞ
phrases.en: This is a little something, if you'd like
phrases.note: Hand the gift over as you say it. No big presentation.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.jp: おせち、一緒に食べましょう
phrases.kana: おせち、いっしょにたべましょう
phrases.note: Osechi is the New Year meal in the stacked boxes. Offering to share is the warm move.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.kana: おもち、おいしいですね
phrases.note: Say it while you eat. If it's in soup, that's お雑煮.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.jp: 今日は呼んでくれて、ありがとうございます
phrases.kana: きょうはよんでくれて、ありがとうございます
phrases.romaji: kyō wa yonde kurete, arigatō gozaimasu
phrases.en: Thank you for having me today
phrases.note: A real thank-you for the visit, once you're comfortable, not at the door.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.jp: お父さんもお母さんも、元気でいてくださいね
phrases.kana: おとうさんもおかあさんも、げんきでいてくださいね
phrases.romaji: otōsan mo okāsan mo, genki de ite kudasai ne
phrases.note: You call them お父さん and お母さん. A soft wish, not a formal speech.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.kana: またらいねんもきますね
phrases.en: I'll come again next year too
phrases.note: ね invites them to agree. Smile when you say it.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.kana: いいおとしを
phrases.en: Have a good rest of the year
phrases.note: For December, before New Year. On the day itself, switch to あけましておめでとう.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

phrases.kana: おしょうがつ、たのしいですね
phrases.note: Say it in the middle of the day, with the food and the visit already going.
phrases.speaker: Rizu

units.title: Family words
units.summary: Talking about family you already know: お父さん / お母さん for his, 父 / 母 for yours, and your younger brother.

phrases.kana: おとうさん
phrases.note: Confirmed: call his dad お父さん. Japanese lifts up other people's family (お〜さん) and stays modest about your own (父, 母).
phrases.grammar: Honorific お〜さん for his parents; modest 父 / 母 for yours.

phrases.kana: おかあさん
phrases.note: Confirmed: call his mom お母さん face to face.

phrases.kana: ちち
phrases.note: The modest word for your own dad. Use it when telling his family about your dad: 父は… (chichi wa…).

phrases.kana: はは
phrases.note: Your own mom, to others. Even Shota's mom calls herself しょうたの母.
Families often say the warmer おじいちゃん (ojiichan). It's fine to use it if they do.
Likewise おばあちゃん (obāchan). Careful: おばさん (obasan, short 'a') means aunt.

phrases.jp: ご両親はお元気ですか
phrases.kana: ごりょうしんはおげんきですか
phrases.note: You'll hear this about your own parents. ご両親 is the polite word for someone else's parents.

phrases.kana: ちちもははもげんきです
phrases.romaji: chichi mo haha mo genki desu
phrases.en: My dad and mom are both well.
phrases.note: Answer with 父 and 母, the modest words for your own parents.
phrases.grammar: A も B も = both A and B.

phrases.kana: おとうとがひとりいます
phrases.note: Confirmed. Modest 弟 for your own younger brother. They may ask 弟さんは元気？

phrases.jp: この方はどなたですか
phrases.kana: このかたはどなたですか
phrases.romaji: kono kata wa donata desu ka
phrases.note: Perfect for the family photo album. Polite 方 (kata) + どなた.

units.title: Home phrases
units.summary: Door-to-bedtime house phrases you'll reuse every visit — casual お邪魔します as a familiar guest.

phrases.kana: おじゃまします
phrases.en: Thank you for having me (as you enter a home)
phrases.note: Literally "I'll be in your way". Say it as you step inside, after taking off your shoes.

phrases.kana: おじゃましました
phrases.en: Thank you for having me (as you leave)
phrases.note: The past-tense version, for when you head home.
Say it when you come back to the house you're staying in. Even as a guest it's warm and welcome.
phrases.grammar: These come in pairs: ただいま ↔ おかえり, 行ってきます ↔ いってらっしゃい.

phrases.note: The reply to ただいま. Family will usually say the casual おかえり.

phrases.kana: いってきます
phrases.note: Said when leaving the house, meaning you'll be back.

phrases.en: Have a good day / Take care
phrases.note: The reply to 行ってきます.
A small thank-you before the first bite. Hands together is a nice touch.

phrases.en: Thank you for the meal (after eating)
phrases.note: Say it to whoever cooked. It means a lot to a mom.
Polite, right for his parents. With Shota or younger cousins, just おやすみ.
Polite, right for his parents and grandparents. They may answer with a casual おはよう; you can keep it polite.

units.title: At the dinner table
units.summary: Kitchen-table talk with family who already know your tastes: compliments, seconds, gentle likes/dislikes.

phrases.note: Say it early and say it often.

phrases.kana: これはなんですか
phrases.note: Asking about a dish shows interest. Families love explaining their food.

phrases.jp: お母さんの料理、大好きです
phrases.kana: おかあさんのりょうり、だいすきです
phrases.en: I love your cooking (said to his mom).
phrases.note: Here お母さん means Shota's mom, so you can say it straight to her.

phrases.jp: もう少しいかがですか
phrases.kana: もうすこしいかがですか
phrases.en: Would you like a little more? (host offers)
phrases.note: You'll also hear the casual おかわりは？ (okawari wa?, "seconds?").
いただきます also means "I'll gratefully accept".

phrases.jp: 少しだけお願いします
phrases.kana: すこしだけおねがいします
phrases.note: A graceful middle ground.

phrases.jp: もうおなかいっぱいです
phrases.note: Soften it: ありがとうございます。でも、もうおなかいっぱいです。
